report_name: 'incransom' Ransomware Claims Attack on Quantum Firm Quantinuum

threat_actors.name: incransom
threat_actors.description: A ransomware group that claimed a successful breach of Quantinuum. The group engages in double extortion and, in this case, accused the victim of hiding the breach during its pre-IPO phase to apply additional pressure.
threat_actors.goals: To receive a ransom payment through double extortion, pressuring the victim by threatening data leaks and making public accusations of corporate misconduct.

malware.name: incransom
malware.description: The ransomware associated with the incransom group, which engages in double extortion by exfiltrating data before encryption.

identities.name: Quantinuum
identities.description: A leading quantum computing company listed on the incransom ransomware group's data leak site. The group claimed to have breached the company during its pre-IPO phase.

indicators.name: Potential Data Staging Tool Execution (7z, rclone)
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Potential Data Staging Tool Execution
id: 9c5b1a3d-8e7f-4b2a-9c8d-6f5e4d3c2b1a
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of 7z.exe or rclone.exe, which are legitimate tools often abused by ransomware groups to compress and exfiltrate data.
references:
  - https://www.galaxywarden.com/blog/breach/quantinuum-com-incransom-2026-08
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-02
tags:
  - attack.t1560.001
  - attack.collection
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\7z.exe'
      - '\rclone.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of 7z.exe or rclone.exe, tools often used by ransomware actors for data staging and exfiltration.

indicators.name: Anomalous Large Data Transfer from R&D Segments
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Large Data Transfer from R&D Segments
id: f8a7b6c5-d4e3-4f2a-1b0c-9d8e7f6a5b4c
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects unusually large data transfers originating from network segments designated for Research & Development (R&D) or source code repositories. This could indicate intellectual property theft.
references:
  - https://www.galaxywarden.com/blog/breach/quantinuum-com-incransom-2026-08
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-02
tags:
  - attack.t1041
  - attack.exfiltration
level: high
logsource:
  category: proxy
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate large data transfers, such as software updates or data backups.
  - Requires tuning with knowledge of baseline traffic patterns and specific IP ranges for R&D segments.
detection:
  selection:
    c-ip: '10.100.0.0/16' # Placeholder for R&D network segment
    sc-bytes_out|gt: 100000000 # Example threshold: 100MB
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects large data transfers from R&D or source code repository servers to external destinations, a key indicator of intellectual property theft.

indicators.name: Anomalous Mass Cloning from Source Code Repository
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Mass Cloning from Source Code Repository
id: e7d6c5b4-a3f2-4e1d-0c9b-8a7f6e5d4c3b
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects anomalous cloning of a large number of repositories by a single user account, especially outside of normal business hours. This requires logs from source code management systems (e.g., GitHub Enterprise, GitLab).
references:
  - https://www.galaxywarden.com/blog/breach/quantinuum-com-incransom-2026-08
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-02
tags:
  - attack.t1119
  - attack.collection
level: medium
logsource:
  category: audit
  service: git
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate developer activity, such as setting up a new development environment.
  - Automated build systems.
detection:
  keywords:
    - 'git-upload-pack'
    - 'clone'
  # This is a conceptual rule. A real implementation would require a SIEM with UEBA capabilities to aggregate clone events per user over a time window and alert on outliers.
  condition: keywords
indicators.description: Detects anomalous cloning of large numbers of repositories by a single user account, especially outside of normal business hours, based on source control logs.
